name: h6-block-held-signal
rationale: Literature-motivated (arXiv:2602.11708). Every hypothesis this pipeline has run has varied WHAT the composite says or HOW FAR the position moves; none has varied how often the composite is allowed to SAY something new. shirube recomputes the composite on every 1-minute bar, which is 6x faster than the fastest timeframe the paper measures and 360x faster than its optimum. The paper reports the same trend-composite construction scoring Sharpe 2.41 at 142 trades/month on 6-hour bars against Sharpe 1.54 at 847 trades/month on 1-hour bars, and attributes the gap to whipsaw in the signal itself rather than to the position-sizing or entry rule — i.e. it claims the SAMPLING FREQUENCY is the defect, independent of the indicator periods. That is a different claim from anything shirube has tested: `rebalance-spacing-15m` (rejected) throttled how often the engine may ACT while leaving the signal free to whipsaw, and `ewma-smoothed-signal-wallclock-30m` (rejected) smoothed the signal continuously rather than holding it, at 1/12 of this horizon. This variant instead quantises the composite onto UTC-aligned 6-hour blocks and holds it constant within a block, while leaving the 60s rebalance cadence, the threshold, the zone mapping and every indicator period byte-identical — so drift-correcting trades against a held target still occur and turnover is not throttled mechanically the way a spacing change throttles it. It also bears directly on the standing no-gross-alpha finding: if a 360x slower signal moves `excess_return_vs_static_mix_pct` toward zero from below, that locates the loss in high-frequency signal noise rather than in the composite's construction.
code_change_summary: Quantise the composite onto fixed UTC-aligned blocks: recompute it only when a new block starts, and hold the previous value for the rest of the block. Three coupled changes, and NONE of them touch TradingEngine::compute_btc_target. (1) src/config.rs: add `pub signal_block_secs: u64` to TradingConfig with `#[serde(default = "default_signal_block_secs")]` returning 0, where 0 means 'no blocking — recompute every bar', i.e. exactly today's behaviour. Set it to 0 in TradingConfig::default(). Extend TradingConfig::validate() to reject a value that is neither 0 nor a positive multiple of 60 (a block shorter than one bar is meaningless at BASE_RESOLUTION = 60), with a Japanese error message matching the surrounding style. Add a unit test that a config JSON lacking the field deserialises to 0. (2) Add one pure helper, `pub(crate) fn block_start(ts: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>, block_secs: u64) -> Option<i64>` on TradingEngine, returning None when block_secs == 0 and otherwise `Some(ts.timestamp().div_euclid(block_secs as i64))` — the index of the UTC-aligned block the timestamp falls in. Document the formula, the alignment guarantee (blocks start at UTC midnight for any block_secs that divides 86400, which 21600 does), and a NOTE citing this hypothesis and arXiv:2602.11708. (3) Apply it at BOTH sites that turn a composite into an allocation target. In src/backtest/simulator.rs::run, carry a `last_block: Option<i64>` and a `held_composite: Option<f64>` alongside the existing `last_rebalance_at` state; on each candle compute the candle's block index from `candle.open_time`, and only call compute_btc_target when the block index differs from `last_block` (or when block_secs is 0), storing the result in `held_composite`; on every other candle reuse `held_composite` unchanged. Feed `held_composite` into the existing `* range_max` + apply_zone + threshold + allocation_delta_to_order path with no other modification, so drift-correcting rebalances against a HELD target still happen every candle exactly as they do today. In src/trading/engine.rs::handle_indicator, carry the same two pieces of state on TradingEngine and apply the identical rule, using the IndicatorOutput's `calculated_at` as the timestamp; when the composite is held, skip the compute_btc_target call and reuse the held value to build the target (do not change the sticky_target semantics — a held composite still updates sticky_target exactly as a freshly computed one would, and a None from compute_btc_target at a block boundary must leave the held value untouched rather than clearing it). Add unit tests covering: block_secs = 0 returns None from block_start; two timestamps 5 minutes apart inside one 6-hour block share a block index; timestamps straddling a 6-hour boundary do not; 21600-second blocks align to 00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00 UTC. In your report, state how many distinct composite values the run produced versus the number of evaluated candles (expect roughly 56 blocks over the 14-day holdout against ~15,400 candles), the realised composite band for both the blocked and unblocked formulas over the identical candles, and `orders_below_min` at all three capitals.
constraints: MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) or its body — this hypothesis changes only HOW OFTEN that function is consulted, so the composite formula is held fixed and the measured effect is attributable to the sampling change alone.

MUST apply the blocking at BOTH call sites (the live site in src/trading/engine.rs::handle_indicator and the backtest site in src/backtest/simulator.rs::run), so the backtest cannot measure a strategy the live engine would not run. NOTE the known live/backtest cadence divergence carried in recent reports: SignalEngine::run republishes every 250 ms live while the backtest evaluates once per 60 s bar, which is exactly why this hypothesis's block boundary MUST be derived from an absolute UTC timestamp rather than from a count of bars or of received signals — a bar-indexed constant would mean something ~240x different live.

MUST default `signal_block_secs` to 0 via serde and in TradingConfig::default(), so a stored config or a hypothesis file lacking the field behaves exactly as today. The baseline run must remain byte-identical to a run of the unmodified code — verify this explicitly and say so in your report.

MUST NOT change TradingEngine::allocation_delta_to_order, the allocation_threshold comparison at any call site, apply_zone, the rebalance_interval_secs spacing logic, the RiskManager call sequence, the exchange lot-size check, the fee logic, or the orders_below_min counting arm. In particular do NOT implement this by raising rebalance_interval_secs — that is a different mechanism which `rebalance-spacing-15m` already tested and which this hypothesis is specifically designed to separate itself from.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the existing compute_btc_target_* tests in src/trading/engine.rs and the simulator tests in src/backtest/simulator.rs — update an expected value only where the new field legitimately changes it (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass).

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically — a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff changes when the allocation target is recomputed on the LIVE order-submission path, per the 'anything touching live trading behavior gets flagged explicitly' rule in docs/self-improvement-loop.md.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the bitFlyer REST/WS client.

paper_reference.title: Systematic Trend-Following with Adaptive Portfolio Construction: Enhancing Risk-Adjusted Alpha in Cryptocurrency Markets
paper_reference.key_claim: For a momentum/trend composite on crypto, the signal's sampling timeframe is itself the binding trade-off rather than the indicator parameters: 6-hour bars delivered Sharpe 2.41 at 142 trades/month while 1-hour bars delivered Sharpe 1.54 at 847 trades/month, with H1/H4 losing to turnover and whipsaw and H8/H12/D1 missing short-lived momentum.
paper_reference.pros: Same asset class and a recent sample (in-sample 2021, out-of-sample Jan 2022 - Dec 2024, 36 months), and it actually models costs (4bp taker fee, size-dependent slippage against 5-minute volume, funding). It speaks to the one dimension shirube has never varied — how often the composite is allowed to change — which is a distinct mechanism from the trade SPACING that `rebalance-spacing-15m` tested and the continuous smoothing that `ewma-smoothed-signal-wallclock-30m` tested, both rejected. It is also a plausible reading of shirube's own standing findings: the strategy loses to its own exposure held statically while turning over ~91x equity per 30 days at the primary capital, and four experiments have shown that widening the composite's band makes things worse, all of which is consistent with high-frequency signal noise rather than a directional error. The change needs no new indicator and no learned model.
paper_reference.cons: Do not trust the numbers here. The instrument is 150+ Binance PERPETUAL SWAPS traded cross-sectionally with a 70/30 long/short split, monthly asset selection by prior-month Sharpe, and ATR trailing stops — shirube is a single-asset BTC/JPY SPOT allocator with no shorting, no asset selection and no stop, so the reported Sharpe is a portfolio-diversification result that cannot transfer to one instrument. Its thresholds were grid-searched in-sample on 2021 and the timeframe comparison in Table 5 is not itself presented as an out-of-sample test, so H6 may be an artifact of that search. Its 4bp taker fee is a third of shirube's 13.6bp effective rate at the 50,000 JPY promotion capital, which changes where the frequency optimum sits. And the doc's own standing finding is that shirube has no measured gross alpha at zero fee, so a mechanism that mainly reduces signal churn can at best move the result toward the static mix; promotion stays gated on shirube's own Sharpe/drawdown/trade-count rule over the holdout, not on the paper's Sharpe.
